Your request to codex-10 at line 2947 quotes C1's finding ("Only 4 of the 23 nodes have agent transcripts"), so the record says which way that link runs. Writing the joined model now.The dead-end list counts the helper variables wrongly. Fixing that one line.㊥ (the six turns as a joined model) The flow joins cleanly into one causal model, and the record settles two things you couldn't see from the buffer alone:
- **The table depends on J1, not J2.** Your request to codex-10 at line 2947 quotes C1's finding ("Only 4 of the 23 nodes have agent transcripts"). So the six-node table traces back through C1 to J1's idea, via the narration. It doesn't go through J2's redirect: J2 fed only C2's plan and C3's proposal.
- **The 🈸 corpus ask went nowhere.** Nothing after it used it, which matches what happened: you said "No".

㊢ (what I built) The probe is `holes/labs/M-diagramprover/flow_23519_probe.clj` (commit `923db1be`):
- **Eight acts, each its own small model:** J1–J3 with 象's readings, C1–C3 with their marks (🖖 read as 🈖), K for your request to codex-10, and N for codex-10's narration.
- **Edges come from what each turn quotes, answers or points to.** I read them off the record by hand; they aren't mined.
- **The join succeeds.** Its only external inputs are "this act happened" for each of the eight, plus the R-node tree's cues.

㊢ (what it computes)
| knocked out | products lost |
|---|---|
| J1 or C1 | all of the rest of the flow |
| K or N | narration, J3's priority, the table, the proposal |
| J3 | priority, table, proposal |
| J2 | redirect, C2's plan, C3's proposal, but not the table |
| C2 | the plan and C3's proposal |

- **Dead ends:** the corpus ask and C3's machine-cues proposal. That proposal was offered and is still unanswered, so it's censored in the mission's sense.
- **Implied independencies:** 78 among the products. One example: given C1's finding, the corpus ask is independent of everything later.

🈖 (what this says about operator intent and agent follow-up) Your exploratory idea paid off through the agent's negative finding, not through your redirect turn. The finding moved into another buffer as your request to codex-10, and that request produced the data. A conversation-only view of J1–C3 would miss this, because the route ran through K in the codex-10 buffer. Two connections to M-aif-over-the-operator:
- the declined ask and the unanswered proposal are the `:declined` and `:no-response` outcomes that mission wants recorded;
- the `🈸:yes` refusals earlier this hour show they currently aren't recorded.

㊟ (limits)
- The edges are my reading of what each turn used; mining wouldn't necessarily give the same graph.
- Values are only "happened or not".
- K and N are in the model only because the turns cite them. Other side channels may exist that I haven't seen.
- The three other files changed in futon3c (`http.clj`, `runner_service*`) belong to another seat. I didn't commit them.

previous_reply_acts.text: (my claim that agent turns have no readings) You're right, and I take it back. My replies already carry their intents in the marks, and each mark's bracket names what it answers. So C1–C3 don't need 象 to read them for intents. The thing missing for agent turns is pattern references only, and the held-out test above is about patterns. The graph has no reply edges because no pattern references are recorded for agent turns, not because the intents are missing.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(two things I found while checking the marks)
- **A wrong mark.** In `*claude-repl:claude-17*`, 28 paragraphs open with 🖖 (U+1F596, a hand gesture) where 🈖 explain was meant. All three "how I'd use it / what I'll do" paragraphs in C1–C3 are among them. That's my error: this session's transcript shows I wrote 🖖 myself at least once. A parser that matches the key would skip those paragraphs. Read correctly, C1 is ㊥ ㊢ 🈖 ㊟ 🈸, C2 is ㊥ 🈖 ㊟, and C3 is ㊥ ㊢ 🈖 ㊟ ㊭.
- **The refused agreement.** This turn's header says "agreement refused: no-visible-offer". That is the gap listed in M-aif-over-the-operator, "Agents post an offer for each 🈸": my 🈸 posted no offer, so your 🈸:yes had nothing to attach to. I acted on it from the text anyway, so the work got done, but the record holds a refusal rather than an agreement.

Each mark has a target, and those targets are the shared names the joined model would use. So step 3, joining the six turns, can go ahead without new readings.
